result.summary: The image shows a residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides, though the right-side walkway is narrow and cluttered with debris. Parallel parking on both sides provides a buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic, but the environment lacks marked crosswalks or traffic calming features.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly shorter individuals, from the view of oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Debris and trash on the right-side sidewalk create physical obstacles and potential tripping hazards.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Marked crossings at intersections would provide pedestrians with a designated and more visible path across the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extending the sidewalk at corners would improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Clearing debris and repairing the walkway surface on the right side would improve accessibility and safety.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly degraded by the absence of a paved sidewalk on the near side and the presence of a large tow truck obstructing the path. A prominent blank building wall further reduces the quality of the space by eliminating passive surveillance and visual interest.

hazards.name: Large vehicle obstruction
hazards.description: A large tow truck is parked on the unpaved shoulder, completely blocking the pedestrian path and sightlines.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk
hazards.description: The near side of the street lacks a paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians onto dirt or into the roadway.

hazards.name: Blank building frontage
hazards.description: A large windowless wall creates a dead space with no passive surveillance or visual interest.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk on the near side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve safety and visibility during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Active Frontage Improvements
interventions.description: Encourage the addition of windows or public art to the blank building wall to improve the pedestrian experience and safety through passive surveillance.

result.summary: The street is a wide, unmarked residential and commercial corridor with sidewalks on both sides but no designated pedestrian crossings. The lack of lane markings and traffic calming measures likely encourages higher vehicle speeds, while parked cars and frequent curb cuts create potential conflict points.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations without priority.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing/Markings
interventions.description: Paint lane lines to define travel lanes and parking lanes, which helps reduce vehicle speeds through psychological narrowing.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a narrow sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. Parked vehicles along the curb create visual obstructions between pedestrians and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the road.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is narrow and directly adjacent to the parking lane with no physical separation or green buffer.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center foreground sidewalk area

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install a vegetated buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility for all road users.
